problem: The answer contradicts the chapter's own arithmetic. With 24 workers each task takes 4 + 0.5 = 4.5 min per worker, so 600 tasks means 25 tasks per worker = 112.5 min, which is roughly half of 225 min. The workers would draw tasks at only 24 ÷ 4.5 ≈ 5.3 tasks/min, far below the master's 40 tasks/min. Dispatching all 600 tasks takes just 15 min, so the master is not a bottleneck and the makespan really would halve. The stated answer is false for the numbers given.
fix: Lower the dispatch rate so the master really binds, e.g. '24 workers would not halve the 225 min makespan if the master can only dispatch 4 tasks per minute': dispatching 600 tasks then needs 150 min, more than the 112.5 min of work the 24 workers can do, so the makespan is about 150 min. Keep the closing line about the slowest stage limiting throughput.

problem: 'Adding workers can hurt: when o is large compared with t, the pool spends its time shuffling tasks, and throughput per worker saturates at 1 ÷ (t + o)' is wrong as written. Overhead o is paid by each worker on its own task, so per-worker throughput is always 1 ÷ (t + o) and total throughput W ÷ (t + o) grows with W; the formula T = N × (t + o) ÷ W never gets worse with more workers. A student will conclude that overhead causes harm from extra workers, which the model does not show.
fix: 'Adding workers stops helping when a shared resource becomes the bottleneck: the master that hands out tasks, the shared file store, or the network. Each worker's own ceiling is 1 ÷ (t + o) tasks per minute, and total throughput is W ÷ (t + o) only until some shared stage saturates. The formula T = N × (t + o) ÷ W has no shared-stage term, so it is optimistic.'

problem: 'The queue is kept short so that one slow task does not leave the other workers idle' is unclear. A short master queue does not by itself protect against a slow task; what helps is keeping each task small and not handing a worker a long batch of tasks in advance.
fix: 'Tasks are kept small, and each worker holds only a small batch at a time, so one slow task delays very little work and the other workers stay busy.'

problem: T = N × (t + o) ÷ W silently assumes N divides evenly by W. With 601 tasks on 12 workers the last worker gets one extra task and the real makespan is one task longer.
fix: Add one line after the formula: 'This holds when N divides evenly by W; otherwise round tasks per worker up to the next whole number.'
